newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London ended slightly firmer as trade buying supported nearby values. December added $1.00 to close at $323.00, while March was up by $1.40 at $320.50. In New York short-covering by funds lifted world raw sugar futures from below unchanged to close just under session peaks.

However, bearish fundamentals are likely to cap any price rise. The International Sugar Organization (ISO) forecast in its September market report a hefty statistical surplus in 1996/97 (October/September) and prices of around 10 cents/lb.

The ISO said a number of factors would restrain the bearish potential of the global balance - but the effect of supply would win through. The ISO said world sugar production should reach 123.8 million tonnes, raw value, in 1996/97 (October/September) 200,000 tonnes up on 1995/96.

It said global consumption was expected to rise by 2.7 million tonnes to 121.3 million tonnes, leaving a statistical surplus of 2.5 million tonnes. However, the market ignored this prediction and March ended 10 points higher at 10.88 cents/lb, while May added 6 points to close at 10.84 cents/lb. The outer months added 5 to 11 points.

ROMANIA - Romania's 1996 sugar production is expected to total 280,000 tonnes, white value, but production will not be enough to cover domestic demand, raising prospects of imports of 120,000 tonnes of raw sugar, Agriculture Minister Alexandro Lapusan, told a news conference.

He added Romania's 1995 beet sugar production was 300,000 tonnes. However, this figure is not in line with official Romanian statistics which put 1995 beet sugar production at around 200,000 tonnes. Hence, it must be assumed that the figures given by the minister contain the production of white sugar from imported raws.

The minister said only 22 out of 30 factories will be operational in 1996 and that his ministry is considering the use of excess capacities at factories to process beets from neighbouring Hungary, Moldova and Yugoslavia.

CHINA - China produced 26,052 tonnes of sugar, raw value, in September 1996, the first month of the 1996/97 campaign, significantly up on last year's figure of 5,000 tonnes. Total production in 1995/96 reached 6.551 million tonnes, up from 5.901 million tonnes produced in 1994/95.

THAILAND - According to trade sources, premiums for Thai raw sugar could rise if the Ministry of Agriculture does reduce its previous estimate of cane production of 60 million tonnes for 1996/97, due to heavy rains. It was added that the next estimate can be expected to be bearish, which will support Thai raw premiums.

INDIA - Sugar exports in September 1996 amounted to 112,187 tonnes, raw value, sharply up on last year's 6,793 tonnes. This brought total exports in 1995/96 (October/September) up to 952,383 tonnes against 37,722 tonnes in 1994/95 and 28,013 tonnes in 1993/94.

Major countries of destination in 1995/96 were Pakistan with 243,379 tonnes whites against nil, Indonesia with 205,810 tonnes compared to nil, Sri Lanka with 177,765 tonnes compared to 16,115 tonnes and Russia with 90,000 tonnes against nil.
Total exports in 1996/97 are not expected to change much from the 1995/96 level unless the government increases the 1 million tonne export quota allotted to the Indian milling sector.

BELGIUM/LUXEMBOURG - Sugar imports in June 1996 amounted to 28,279 tonnes, raw value, down from last year's 82,626 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first three quarters of 1995/96 (October/June) up to 623,965 tonnes compared to 907,661 tonnes in the like period of the previous year.

Total exports in 1994/95 amounted to 1.14 million tonnes against 663,985 tonnes in 1993/94. Major countries of origin in October/June 1995/96 were France with 460,516 tonnes whites against 741,906 tonnes, Germany with 66,722 tonnes compared to 64,859 tonnes and the Netherlands with 38,947 tonnes, up from 11,814 tonnes.

Sugar exports in June 1996 reached 49,503 tonnes, sharply down from last year's 191,062 tonnes. This brought cumulative exports in October/June 1995/96 up to 885,802 tonnes against 1.35 million tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total exports in 1994/95 amounted to 1.57 million tonnes against 1.34 million tonnes in 1993/94.

Major countries of destination in October/June 1995/96 were Syria with 129,997 tonnes whites against 113,486 tonnes, Turkey with 100,738 tonnes against 80,126 tonnes and Israel with 96,687 tonnes compared to 77,918 tonnes.
